items.title: Terry Gibbs interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, November 5, 2021 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: God, he could have called Teddy, he could have called fifty — this was like heaven when he called, you know.

ctx.x: Yes. So we’ve been at this for about an hour, I’ve really enjoyed this. I want to wrap up with a couple of questions. I wonder if you could have done anything else in your life besides being a musician.

You know I did want to be a boxer at one time but it was either that — but I realized playing music was more important to me. I don’t think there’s anything I actually wanted to do that, you know something Monk? I may have had a lot of mishaps but we all — I’m 97 years old now and we all have had some rainy days. You know. But I am blessed with being, in my 97 years maybe two years of it I would say were dumb, were just something — it’s not I regret, it’s something I couldn’t do anything about. There was a point…

blessed as I was. If you look at the pictures in the book, all those people, first of all Benny Goodman was the King of Swing. When I was 25 years old and he was 42 I played with Benny. After four bars we were the same age. Music has no numbers. Same age. I mean I wrote about this, not only did I play with Charlie Parker but he worked for me one time for four weeks. But Dizzy Gillespie, who was my friend, who heard me play because I worked opposite him a lot of time, I was sitting by a music store when I was…
